title: The Stockade
body: The Stockade is the prison of Stormwind, a high-security complex hidden beneath the canal district, its gate opening on the northern stretch of the canal that rings the Mage Quarter. Thieves, political agitators and killers are all held here, but the guards no longer hold the place. The Defias among the inmates have risen in revolt and driven the guards out, and now prisoners, convicts and insurgents of the Brotherhood roam free through the halls in their red bandanas. From the gate a long hall leads inward, and beyond it the cell blocks stretch away on either hand. Some of the inmates are more than faces in the crowd. An orc called Targorr the Dread waits at the end of the long hall, and deep in the southern block, among the Brotherhood's insurgents, stands a man named Bazil Thredd. Few go in by choice. Outside the gate the warden paces and frets, unable to understand how his prison was lost so suddenly, and afraid of what the Captain will say when he hears.

parts.body: Not every rioter in the Stockade is human. A dwarf named Bruegal Ironknuckle had thrown in his lot with the Defias in the cell blocks, and he fought at their side as fiercely as any of them. It did not save him. The dwarf fell among the rioters he had joined.

title: Targorr the Dread
body: Targorr the Dread is an orc, one of the inmates of the Stockade, and the riot has left him as free as any of the men around him. He stands among the rioters at the far end of the long hall that leads in from the gate, a sword in each hand, and anyone who means to go deeper into the prison must pass him. What brought an orc to a cell beneath Stormwind, and how he earned his name, the halls themselves do not say.

parts.body: In Lakeshire his name is not forgotten. Targorr served the Blackrock warlord Gath'Ilzogg as his supreme executioner, and men who fought bravely to defend the kingdom were tortured at his whim. Taken at last, he was locked in the Stockade under sentence of death.

title: Hamhock
body: Hamhock is a two-headed ogre, and one of the strangest prisoners the Stockade holds. He is no man of the Brotherhood, but the riot has made allies of unlikely cellmates, and he has thrown in his lot with the Defias. He stands deep in the southern cell block among the Brotherhood's insurgents, a heavy cleaver in his fist, not far from where Bazil Thredd holds out at the far end of the block.

parts.body: Hamhock met intruders with a bellow that he would crush them. He hurled lightning that leapt from one foe to the next, and worked himself into a bloodlust that drove his blows faster, but none of it was enough. The two-headed ogre went down at last among the insurgents he had joined.

title: Quell the Uprising
body: Outside the Stockade gate, Warden Thelwater still cannot understand how he lost his prison. The prisoners were suddenly everywhere at once, he says, and someone must have helped them. He fears for his post as much as for the city: if word gets out that the prison is overrun he will lose his job, and if the Captain hears of it, it will be the end of him. Whatever foul play lies behind it, the first task is to force the prisoners back into submission for the safety of Stormwind. The punishment for insurgency is death, and he wants the Defias prisoners, convicts and insurgents cut down until the uprising is under control.

parts.body: More than two dozen of the rioters died in the Stockade's halls, and Thelwater was thankful to the one who had shown such force there. But he could see now that the trouble ran deeper than a few unruly prisoners. This problem, he admitted, was bigger than the both of them.

title: What Comes Around
body: In Lakeshire, Guard Berton has not forgotten Targorr the Dread, the orc who served Gath'Ilzogg as his executioner and tortured men who fought bravely for the kingdom. Targorr is held in the Stormwind Stockade under sentence of death, yet the sentence has not been carried out: one of the nobles in the capital has put a hold on the execution. Berton is sure that foul play is at work, and he will not wait to see what comes of it. He wants someone to go to the Stockade and behead the orc before any trickery can come to his aid.

parts.body: Targorr's head came back to Lakeshire. Berton was glad of it, and glad that the orc had learned at the end what it was to be on the other side of the executioner's work. Sometimes, he said, the truest justice can only be found outside the courtroom, beyond the reach of nobles and their politics.

title: The Color of Blood
body: In Old Town, Nikova Raskol carries a grief that has gone cold and bitter. Her grandson Mac was only fourteen. When the army was sent off to the front he took up arms to defend the city, and he served as a guard in the Stockade, where the Defias gang is locked up. Mac scolded some of the prisoners for tearing up their wool blankets to make scarves, the mark of their gang, and for that they stabbed him in the back. Nikova wants revenge, and she has named its token: ten of the gang's precious wool bandanas, red as blood.

parts.body: Ten red wool bandanas, taken from the Defias in the Stockade, came back to Old Town. Nikova saw only waste in them. These filthy rags were what her grandson had died for. She could not undo the past, she said, but the one who brought them had won her family justice.
